cases.question: This month the VAT I paid on purchases is more than the VAT I collected on sales. What happens to the extra?

claims.text: Where input VAT exceeds output VAT, a taxable person is entitled to use the excess tax as a credit against subsequent months. This applies not later than the due date for rendering the relevant tax return prescribed by the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025.
A taxable person is entitled to a refund of excess VAT not used as a credit, upon request to the Service and provision of such information or documents as the Service may require.
VAT a taxable person pays to a supplier on taxable supplies made to the person is called input VAT, and VAT collected on making taxable supplies is called output VAT.

Input tax on a taxable supply to a registered person may be deducted from the tax payable on its taxable supplies at the end of the tax period in which the supply occurred, but only to the extent it was incurred for consumption, use or supply in the course of making taxable supplies.
Where input tax is incurred in making both taxable and non-taxable supplies, only the proportion relating to making taxable supplies may be deducted.
Input tax is allowable for deduction within five years after the end of the tax period in which it was incurred.
The input tax that may be deducted is limited to taxable supplies made as from the commencement of the Act.

Where input VAT exceeds output VAT, a taxable person is entitled to use the excess tax as a credit against subsequent months. This applies not later than the due date for rendering the relevant tax return prescribed by the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

A taxable person is entitled to a refund of excess VAT not used as a credit, upon request to the Service and provision of such information or documents as the Service may require. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

VAT a taxable person pays to a supplier on taxable supplies made to the person is called input VAT, and VAT collected on making taxable supplies is called output VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 152; Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 154]

Input tax on a taxable supply to a registered person may be deducted from the tax payable on its taxable supplies at the end of the tax period in which the supply occurred, but only to the extent it was incurred for consumption, use or supply in the course of making taxable supplies. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

Where input tax is incurred in making both taxable and non-taxable supplies, only the proportion relating to making taxable supplies may be deducted. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

Input tax is allowable for deduction within five years after the end of the tax period in which it was incurred. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

The input tax that may be deducted is limited to taxable supplies made as from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156 (gazette pages A 474, A 475)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 152 (gazette page A 473)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 154 (gazette page A 474)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156: The gazette lets a person whose supplies are zero-rated pay VAT on its inputs and then claim a refund; the National Assembly text has no such subsection. (DR-067)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156: Because of the gazette's extra subsection (4), gazette (5) and (6) are National Assembly (4) and (5). (DR-068)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 154: Cross-reference: the rate is in section 148 (gazette); the National Assembly text cites section 146, which is not its rate section (147). (DR-061)
